hypothesis: To determine whether incorporating a spatial lag model into a machine learning framework for predicting PM2.5 concentrations improves prediction accuracy compared to models using only temporal features, as measured by reduced mean absolute error on the UCI Air Quality dataset.
author: coder-agent
baseline: Performance of a Random Forest model trained exclusively on temporal features
success_criteria: If the MAE of the model incorporating spatial lag is lower than that of the temporal-only model, the hypothesis is supported. Conversely, if the MAE is higher or similar, the hypothesis is refuted.
notes: Temporal-only model MAE: 83.2963. Spatial model MAE: 89.8782. Spatial model does not show improvement.
